title: What might have been
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THE PAST IS MARKED TWICE. L3-M4's -(eu)myeon does not change at all; what makes a condition impossible is a PAST stem on both halves. Gamyeon joayo is an open condition, gasseumyeon joasseul geoyeyo one that did not happen.

ENGLISH PUTS THE UNREALITY IN THE AUXILIARY. Had gone, would have seen — so a learner marks the helper and writes gal geoyeosseoyo. Korean marks the STEM and leaves geoyeyo exactly as L1-M6 taught it: gasseul geoyeyo.

V-(eu)l geol geuraesseoyo IS THE REGRET PROPER, and it is only ever about the speaker's OWN past action. It is never used of what somebody else did, and geol is a bound noun that never stands on its own.

-eosseoya haesseoyo SAYS HAD TO, NOT SHOULD HAVE. Ilchik gasseoya haesseoyo is I had to go early as readily as I should have gone early, and only context chooses. The unambiguous regret is ilchik gal geol geuraesseoyo.
THE NEGATIVE REGRET PUTS an IN FRONT OF THE MODIFIER, never in front of geuraesseoyo. An bol geol geuraesseoyo is I should not have watched it; bol geol an geuraesseoyo is not a sentence at all.

ENGLISH IF IS ONE WORD FOR TWO CONDITIONS. The open one and the impossible one look identical, so the past marking is the only difference a learner can see: bi-ga omyeon an gayo against bi-ga wasseumyeon an gasseul geoyeyo.

NOTHING NEARLY HAPPENED HERE. The nearly frame is L5's, and L3-M9's -deon stays a remembered habit: a regret is not a memory. geuttae is one word, back then, and the time clause proper waits for L4-M6.

sentences.cue: It would have been good if I had gone early back then.

words.note: One word, not geu plus ttae. It plants the past moment the rest of the sentence undoes, and it is what tells a listener the condition is closed rather than open.
L3-M4's -(eu)myeon on a PAST stem: gasseoyo plus the ending. Gamyeon is if I go; gasseumyeon is if I had gone, and nothing else marks the difference.
joasseoyo under the -(eu)l modifier, waiting for geoyeyo. The pair joasseul geoyeyo is how Korean says it would have been better.

sentences.trap: Both halves carry the past or neither counts. Gasseumyeon joayo mixes an impossible if with a present outcome and lands nowhere.
sentences.sound: GEU-ttae IL-jjik GA-sseu-myeon JO-a-sseul geo-YE-yo. The tt of geuttae is tensed, and the double s of gasseumyeon is held before the ending.

variations.cue: It would have been good if I had come early back then.
variations.changed: coming rather than going, with the same doubled past

variations.cue: It would have been good if I had taken the medicine back then.
variations.changed: a different regret in the same frame

mistake.why: gamyeon is the open condition, if I go. A closed one needs the past on the if-half too: gasseumyeon.

sentences.usage: Looking back on a day that went wrong, with a friend.

sentences.display: Bi-ga an wasseumyeon chukje-e gasseul geoyeyo.
sentences.script: 비가 안 왔으면 축제에 갔을 거예요.
sentences.cue: If it had not rained, I would have gone to the festival.
sentences.literal: rain-SUBJ not came-if festival-to went-would thing-is

words.note: The past conditional of wayo. With bi-ga in front it is if it had rained, and the an before it negates the rain, not the condition.
gasseoyo under the -(eu)l modifier. It cannot stand alone: gasseul geoyeyo is the whole form, and geoyeyo is L1-M6's, unchanged.

sentences.trap: English says if it had not rained and marks nothing else. Korean marks the outcome too, so gasseul geoyeyo and not gal geoyeyo.
sentences.sound: BI-ga AN WA-sseu-myeon CHUK-je-e GA-sseul geo-YE-yo. an leans into wasseumyeon as one breath.

variations.display: Bi-ga an wasseumyeon hakgyo-e gasseul geoyeyo.
variations.script: 비가 안 왔으면 학교에 갔을 거예요.
variations.cue: If it had not rained, I would have gone to school.
variations.changed: the destination

variations.display: Bi-ga wasseumyeon chukje-e an gasseul geoyeyo.
variations.script: 비가 왔으면 축제에 안 갔을 거예요.
variations.cue: If it had rained, I would not have gone to the festival.
variations.changed: the negative moved to the outcome half

mistake.display: Bi-ga an omyeon chukje-e gasseul geoyeyo.
mistake.script: 비가 안 오면 축제에 갔을 거예요.
mistake.why: omyeon is if it rains, still open. The rain is over and did happen, so the if-half takes the past: wasseumyeon.

sentences.usage: Explaining a missed outing the next day.

words.note: A bound noun, geot plus -eul worn down to one syllable. It never stands alone and only ever follows a -(eu)l modifier: gal geol, bol geol, meogeul geol.
Literally it was so, but after V-(eu)l geol it does the regretting and nothing else. Gal geol geuraesseoyo is one frame; the halves are never separated.

sentences.trap: This is the unambiguous regret. Ilchik gasseoya haesseoyo would be heard first as I had to go early, which is a different claim.
sentences.sound: IL-jjik GAL GEOL geu-RAE-sseo-yo. geol is short and unstressed; it leans onto gal in front of it.

variations.cue: I should have eaten early.
variations.changed: a different verb under the same modifier

variations.cue: I should have studied early.
variations.changed: studying rather than going

mistake.why: The modifier in front of geol is the plain -(eu)l, gal. geuraesseoyo already carries the past, and marking it twice here is one past too many.

sentences.usage: Muttered to yourself after a long queue.
sentences.mnemonic: gal geol: plain modifier, past regret.

sentences.display: Geu yeonghwa-reul an bol geol geuraesseoyo.
sentences.script: 그 영화를 안 볼 걸 그랬어요.
sentences.cue: I should not have watched that film.
sentences.literal: that film-OBJ not watch-ing thing was-so

words.note: L1-M3's negative, in the one position this frame allows: in front of the -(eu)l modifier. An bol geol geuraesseoyo is I should not have watched it.

sentences.trap: The negative belongs to bol, not to geuraesseoyo. Moving it to the end gives bol geol an geuraesseoyo, which is not a sentence.
sentences.sound: GEU yeong-HWA-reul AN BOL GEOL geu-RAE-sseo-yo. an and bol run together as an-bol.

variations.display: Geu chaek-eul an bol geol geuraesseoyo.
variations.script: 그 책을 안 볼 걸 그랬어요.
variations.cue: I should not have read that book.
variations.changed: the book; bol covers reading as well as watching

variations.cue: I should have watched that film.
variations.changed: the regret turned round, with no an

mistake.display: Geu yeonghwa-reul bol geol an geuraesseoyo.
mistake.script: 그 영화를 볼 걸 안 그랬어요.
mistake.why: an negates the modifier, never geuraesseoyo. The negative sits in front of bol: an bol geol geuraesseoyo.

sentences.usage: Coming out of a cinema you wish you had skipped.

sentences.cue: I had to go home early yesterday.

words.note: L2-M8's -eoya on a PAST stem. It says had to, not should have, so it needs a context; the regret with no ambiguity in it is gal geol geuraesseoyo.

sentences.trap: -eosseoya haesseoyo is the obligation frame in the past, and English hears should have in it. Only what surrounds it decides which reading is meant.
sentences.sound: EO-je IL-jjik JI-be GA-sseo-ya HAE-sseo-yo. The p of jip runs into the -e, so it is heard as ji-be.

variations.cue: I had to go to the hospital early yesterday.
variations.changed: the destination

variations.cue: I had to take the medicine yesterday.
variations.changed: the same frame on a different verb

mistake.why: haesseoyo, not haeyo. The obligation is over with the day, so hada carries the past as well.

sentences.usage: Accounting for yesterday to a colleague.

sentences.cue: If I had taken the medicine, I would have been fine.

words.cue: if I had taken · if I had eaten
words.note: The past conditional of meogeoyo. Korean takes medicine by eating it, so yak-eul meogeosseumyeon is if I had taken the medicine.
L2-M1's gwaenchanayo in the past under the -(eu)l modifier. It is the mildest outcome word and the one a learner reaches for most often.

sentences.trap: L2-M8 taught yak-eul meogeoyo for taking medicine, and the counterfactual changes nothing about that: only the stem's tense moves.
sentences.sound: YA-geul meo-GEO-sseu-myeon gwaen-CHA-na-sseul geo-YE-yo. The k of yak runs into the -eul, so it is heard as ya-geul.

variations.cue: If I had taken the medicine, I would have gone to school.
variations.changed: a different outcome

variations.cue: If I had taken the medicine back then, I would have been fine.
variations.changed: geuttae in front, pinning the missed moment

mistake.why: meogeumyeon is if I take it, an open condition. The closed one needs the past on the stem: meogeosseumyeon.

sentences.usage: Telling a friend why the cold dragged on.

sentences.display: Jeongmal huhoehaeyo. Deo gongbuhal geol geuraesseoyo.
sentences.script: 정말 후회해요. 더 공부할 걸 그랬어요.
sentences.cue: I really regret it. I should have studied more.
sentences.literal: really regret. more study-ing thing was-so

words.note: The word for the feeling, said in the present even about a long-past thing. It names the regret; V-(eu)l geol geuraesseoyo is what the regret is about.

sentences.trap: huhoehaeyo names a feeling and cannot take the regretted action after it the way English regret can. The action goes in its own geol geuraesseoyo sentence.
sentences.sound: JEONG-mal hu-HOE-hae-yo. DEO GONG-bu-hal GEOL geu-RAE-sseo-yo. hoe is one beat, close to English hway.

variations.display: Jeongmal huhoehaeyo. Deo ilhal geol geuraesseoyo.
variations.script: 정말 후회해요. 더 일할 걸 그랬어요.
variations.cue: I really regret it. I should have worked more.
variations.changed: working rather than studying

variations.display: Jeongmal huhoehaesseoyo. Deo gongbuhal geol geuraesseoyo.
variations.script: 정말 후회했어요. 더 공부할 걸 그랬어요.
variations.cue: I really regretted it. I should have studied more.
variations.changed: the regret itself put in the past

mistake.display: Jeongmal huhoehaeyo. Deo gongbuhaesseul geol geuraesseoyo.
mistake.script: 정말 후회해요. 더 공부했을 걸 그랬어요.
mistake.why: The modifier in front of geol is the plain -(eu)l: gongbuhal. geuraesseoyo is already the past half of the frame.

sentences.usage: After results come out, to someone close.
sentences.mnemonic: Name the feeling, then name the deed.

sentences.cue: It would have been good if I had booked back then.

words.note: The past conditional of haeyo, and the one that carries every hada compound: yeyak-eul haesseumyeon, jeonhwa-reul haesseumyeon, gongbu-reul haesseumyeon.

sentences.trap: L4-M1's yeyak takes hada, so the whole counterfactual rides on haesseumyeon; there is no separate booking verb to conjugate.
sentences.sound: GEU-ttae ye-YA-geul HAE-sseu-myeon JO-a-sseul geo-YE-yo. The k of yeyak runs into the -eul.

variations.cue: It would have been good if I had called back then.
variations.changed: calling rather than booking

variations.cue: It would have been good if I had booked.
variations.changed: geuttae dropped; the doubled past alone still closes it

mistake.why: hamyeon is if I do, still open. The closed condition is haesseumyeon, and geuttae cannot do that work on its own.

sentences.mnemonic: geuttae sets the scene; the past does the work.

sentences.cue: If I had taken a taxi, I would not have been late.

words.note: The past conditional of tayo, the verb for boarding. A taxi, a bus and a train are all ridden with it, and the vehicle takes -eul or -reul.
neujeosseoyo under the -(eu)l modifier. With an in front it is the outcome that did not happen: an neujeosseul geoyeyo.

sentences.trap: The an here negates the outcome, not the condition. In S02's frame the same an sat on the if-half instead, and the two positions say opposite things.
sentences.sound: TAEK-si-reul TA-sseu-myeon AN neu-JEO-sseul geo-YE-yo. an leans into neujeosseul as one breath.

variations.cue: If I had taken the subway, I would not have been late.
variations.changed: the subway instead of the taxi

variations.cue: If I had taken the bus, I would not have been late.
variations.changed: the bus instead of the taxi

mistake.why: neujeul geoyeyo is a prediction about a day still ahead. The half that did not happen needs the past under the modifier: neujeosseul.

sentences.usage: Apologising for arriving late to a meeting.
sentences.mnemonic: Ride in the past, arrive in the past.

sentences.cue: I should have taken the medicine. That is why I regret it.

words.cue: should have taken · had to take
words.note: The -eosseoya haesseoyo frame on meogeoyo. Like gasseoya it reads as had to first, and the huhoehaeyo after it is what settles the sentence as a regret.

sentences.trap: This is the module's slogan trap. -eosseoya haesseoyo alone does not mean should have; the second sentence is what makes the reading a regret.
sentences.sound: YA-geul meo-GEO-sseo-ya HAE-sseo-yo. geu-RAE-seo hu-HOE-hae-yo. The second sentence drops in pitch throughout.

variations.cue: I should have gone early. That is why I regret it.
variations.changed: the same pair of sentences on going

variations.cue: I should have taken the medicine. I really regret it.
variations.changed: jeongmal instead of the causal geuraeseo

mistake.why: The regret frame ends in geuraesseoyo, not haesseoyo: meogeul geol geuraesseoyo. haesseoyo belongs to the -eosseoya frame instead.

sentences.usage: Owning up to a small piece of carelessness.
sentences.mnemonic: Had to, plus regret, equals should have.
